title: spec(kernel): two capability tokens resolved by the cloud runtime loader — `audit-compliance` and `access-policy-console` — beside `governance`
body:
repo:cloud#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbYK6SZCmyzbGnrvmkk

Filing gate: ① a measured gap with file:line. A cloud consumer cannot finish without it. Found by the objectstack-ai/cloud#4197 card (report 6754912022, `out_of_scope_findings`) at cloud's pin `e24136c2`. It is the same on `main`.

## Gap

`packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts`:
- `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS` (L31) lists `governance` among the tokens "resolved by cloud's objectos-runtime loader only" (L80–83).
- `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` (L171) has the matching rows.

The cloud runtime has two more per-environment capabilities that a tenant kernel should be able to `require` the same way. Without a token they cannot be declared or mounted per environment, so cloud has to mark them unavailable on its hosted shape. That is recorded on cloud as a gap, not a product decision.

## Ask

1. Add `audit-compliance` and `access-policy-console` to `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS`, in the cloud-loader-only group beside `governance`.
2. Add their `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` rows with `edition: 'cloud'` and a note in the same shape as `governance`'s. Use the provider package names that cloud's loader resolves, and ask the cloud lane if they are not readable here.
3. Keep `serve-capability-vocabulary.test.ts` (the 1:1 drift test) green.

This adds accepted `requires` values, so it is a published-schema change: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, owed the contract review tier.

## Consumer

objectstack-ai/cloud: after a pin that contains this, cloud's loader adds the two `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` entries, and the hosted catalog column flips from "no" to "yes". That is a cloud card the cloud lane files when this lands.
